phase3_findings.description: The blank-string coercion accepts an empty or whitespace-only value for save_text_memories and reads it as off, while the sibling booleans exposed through the same MCPB ${user_config.<bool>} mapping (MemoryConfig.save_queries, allow_import, allow_admin_tools, DatabaseConfig.read_only) have no such coercion and raise a validation error at startup instead. The final pass adds the related case of a bundle upgraded from a version predating the field, where an unreplaced ${user_config.save_text_memories} placeholder blocks server startup rather than reading as off. No decided criterion asks for either behavior.

The internal docs claim the prompt's section numbered 2. TEXT MEMORY is not printed when the flag is off, repeated at docs/internal/setup/config-loading.md line 30, but the new assertions in tests/unit/test_factory_wiring.py lines 483, 498 and 513 match only the bare text TEXT MEMORY, so the section-number half of the claim has no test behind it. The claim itself holds against src/sqllens/agent/core/system_prompt/default.py.

The new eight-line comment names the wrong change and its consequence only in its last three lines; the first five restate what save_text_memory is for and how has_text_memory gates the prompt section, which docs/internal/agent/memory.md already records. The comment is accurate. Reported in the previous iteration with no decision recorded and still present at this head.

The pre-existing save_queries comment still says dropping the registration drops the prompt guidance with it, which is the claim this change corrects for the text-memory case in docs/internal/agent/memory.md line 96 and docs/internal/setup/config-loading.md line 30, because the save sentence rides on has_search and survives. The diff mirrors the corrected wording into the new comment but leaves this sibling comment unchanged. The line is outside the diff and is an internal code comment, so it is a clarity gap only.
